newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida workers vote to continue strike.
newsitem.headline: Escondida workers vote to continue strike.

text.p: Unionized workers at Chile's Escondida copper mine voted 131 to 127 to accept a company wage offer but the margin was not enough to end the dispute and the strike will continue, a union official said Wednesday.
"The strike continues," Pablo Godoy of the Chilean Mining Confederation told Reuters by telephone.
He explained that union rules specified that the more than 100 workers who did not vote are counted as supporting the strike.
Godoy said he did not know why so many strikers failed to turn up to vote.
"The next step will be to hold more demonstrations and demand that the company improve their offer," he said, speaking from a bakers' union office borrowed for the vote by the Escondida union.
The 358 unionized workers at Escondida began striking Friday to demand wage increases. The rest of the mine's 2,000-strong workforce did not join the strike.
Mine CEO Ken Pickering said Wednesday that production was normal and shipments unaffected by the strike.
